purpose: W6-C: define provider-neutral EDO and EPD transport/receipt/conformance authority over canonical immutable documents and signature evidence without activating any vendor or treating transport as legal finality.
authorization: Owner instruction on 2026-09-05 to continue PC-CROP. Staged only; implementation authority requires separate governance review/merge and immutable scope promotion.
requiredInvariants: Canonical document bytes/version/hash and signature evidence remain the source of legal document identity. EDO/EPD transport never creates or mutates document content authority.

DocumentTransportPort is provider-neutral and exposes capability/version negotiation, send, status query, receipt ingestion, cancellation/correction transport and webhook/inbox semantics without vendor-specific core fields.

Transport states are distinct from canonical document lifecycle. REQUEST_ACCEPTED/QUEUED/SENT_TO_PROVIDER is never DELIVERED/ACCEPTED/SIGNED until a validated immutable provider/legal receipt proves the exact state transition.

Every outbound envelope binds exact document id/version/hash, sender/recipient organization authority, signature receipt references, document type/profile, idempotency key and provider integration binding.

Every inbound receipt binds provider/integration account, external event/document id, exact payload fingerprint, provider timestamp, receipt type/status and verification result. Replay or cross-provider mismatch fails closed.

EPD/ETRN conformance is versioned and explicit. A provider-specific payload maps to a canonical transport-document profile only if required fields, identities, signatures and schema/profile versions validate.
One provider may support EDO but not EPD/ETRN or vice versa. Missing capability fails closed and cannot silently fall back to upload or another provider unless an authorized routing decision is made.
At least two test/reference provider implementations must satisfy the same port to prove multi-provider substitution without changing Document/Deal core.
External adapters remain NOT_ACTIVATED without real contract, credentials, endpoints, webhook secrets/certificates and accepted production receipts. Fixtures cannot claim legal delivery.
Provider outage/degradation preserves durable retry/inbox/outbox evidence and does not mutate canonical document finality.
ATI document transport, if used, is merely another provider route and cannot bypass EPD/signature/document conformance.
Registration, Role Eligibility, Federal Accounting lock #4321, W3/W5 document/signature authority, packages/lockfiles and REG.RU production topology remain unchanged.
acceptance: Contract tests prove provider-neutral send/status/receipt/webhook models and no vendor-specific core field leakage.
Two reference providers can transport the same canonical document profile without modifying Document core or lifecycle policy.
Queued/request-accepted states cannot produce DELIVERED/ACCEPTED; only validated immutable receipts can.
Wrong document hash/version, recipient/sender, integration binding, event replay, stale/invalid webhook or signature mismatch fails closed.
EPD/ETRN conformance tests cover valid/invalid profile versions, missing mandatory fields and signature/identity mismatches.
NOT_ACTIVATED adapters cannot fabricate success and no secret/credential is committed.
Provider outage/retry does not duplicate sends or rewrite historical transport receipts.
Exact-head review plus real REG.RU provider credentialed acceptance is required before EDO/EPD/ATI_DOKI terminal credit.
remainingTerminalBoundary: Real EDO/EPD provider contracts, credentials, endpoint/schema documentation and webhook/certificate setup are external dependencies.
W3-B document lifecycle and W5-B signer authority must be consumer-wired before legal delivery can become end-to-end PASS.
At least two real production providers are required for terminal multi-provider evidence; reference fakes are foundation evidence only.
REG.RU production receipts and operational failure/reconciliation evidence remain mandatory.
